subject: Physics
title: Grade 9 Olympiad Physics Core 1A Ontology: Vectors, Coordinate Frames & Geometric Invariants

structural_pillars.name: Geometric Invariance & Vector Identity
structural_pillars.statement: A physical vector represents an objective geometric entity possessing magnitude and spatial orientation, independent of the Cartesian frame chosen to measure it.
structural_pillars.mathematical_invariant: |A|^2 = A_x^2 + A_y^2 = A_{x'}^2 + A_{y'}^2 (Scalar norm is preserved under rigid spatial coordinate rotations)
structural_pillars.scope_condition: Euclidean 3D space with flat Riemannian metric.

structural_pillars.name: Orthogonal Basis Decomposition & Coordinate Projections
structural_pillars.statement: Any coplanar vector A can be resolved into a unique linear combination of mutually perpendicular unit vectors: A = A_x i_hat + A_y j_hat, where A_x = |A| cos theta and A_y = |A| sin theta.
structural_pillars.mathematical_invariant: i_hat . j_hat = 0, |i_hat| = |j_hat| = 1; Angle theta must strictly reference the declared adjacent axis

structural_pillars.name: Vector Space Linear Superposition
structural_pillars.statement: Vectors combine according to geometric head-to-tail triangle law or equivalent parallelogram law; resultant vector magnitude is bounded by the triangle inequality |A - B| <= |R| <= A + B.
structural_pillars.mathematical_invariant: R^2 = A^2 + B^2 + 2 A B cos theta; tan beta = (B sin theta) / (A + B cos theta)
structural_pillars.scope_condition: Concurrent vectors acting on a single point particle or rigid body center of mass.

structural_pillars.name: Galilean Relative Kinematics & Observer Subtraction
structural_pillars.statement: The velocity of object A as perceived by observer B is obtained by subtracting the observer's velocity vector: v_{AB} = v_A - v_B. To transform to frame B, apply -v_B to all entities.
structural_pillars.mathematical_invariant: v_{AB} = - v_{BA}; v_{AC} = v_{AB} + v_{BC} (Transitive Galilean velocity chain rule)
structural_pillars.scope_condition: Inertial and accelerating reference frames at non-relativistic speeds (v << c).

structural_pillars.name: Metric Products: Scalar Projection & Vector Normal Generation
structural_pillars.statement: The scalar (dot) product evaluates parallel projection and physical work (W = F . d = |F||d| cos theta), while vector (cross) product generates a perpendicular pseudo-vector representing rotational moment or torque (tau = r x F = |r||F| sin theta n_hat).
structural_pillars.mathematical_invariant: A . B = B . A (Commutative); A x B = -(B x A) (Antisymmetric); A perp B <=> A . B = 0; A || B <=> A x B = 0
structural_pillars.scope_condition: Dot product maps V x V -> R; Cross product is uniquely defined in 3D Euclidean space.

cognitive_conflict_matrix.intuitive_misconception: If displacement A is 4 m and displacement B is 3 m, the resultant displacement must be 7 m.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.newtonian_scientific_truth: The resultant depends on the spatial angle theta: R = sqrt(4^2 + 3^2 + 2(4)(3) cos theta). It can range anywhere between 1 m (antiparallel) and 7 m (collinear). For orthogonal displacements, R = 5 m.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.decisive_experiment: Walking 4 meters East then 3 meters North. Direct laser measurement to origin confirms 5 meters net displacement, not 7 meters.

cognitive_conflict_matrix.intuitive_misconception: A negative vector component (e.g., -10 m/s) represents a smaller physical magnitude or a 'defective' speed compared to +2 m/s.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.newtonian_scientific_truth: The sign designates direction relative to an arbitrary declared coordinate axis. An object moving at -10 m/s has five times the speed (kinetic energy) of one moving at +2 m/s; it simply travels in the opposite direction.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.decisive_experiment: Flipping coordinate convention (+x pointing West instead of East) instantly changes the sign of all velocity components without modifying the physical motion of vehicles.

cognitive_conflict_matrix.intuitive_misconception: Horizontal component is always cos theta and vertical component is always sin theta.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.newtonian_scientific_truth: The trigonometric function is governed by the triangle geometry: the side adjacent to angle theta receives cos theta, while the side opposite receives sin theta. If theta is measured from the vertical, vertical component is A cos theta and horizontal is A sin theta.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.decisive_experiment: Resolving gravity weight along an inclined plane where incline angle theta is measured from horizontal: normal force perpendicular to incline is mg cos theta, not mg sin theta.

cognitive_conflict_matrix.intuitive_misconception: If an object travels along a circular path at a constant speed of 10 m/s, its change in velocity is zero because its speed does not change.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.newtonian_scientific_truth: Velocity is a vector. Changing direction changes the vector state even if magnitude is constant: Delta v = v_f - v_i. For a 90-degree turn at speed v, |Delta v| = v sqrt(2) != 0, requiring a continuous net centripetal force.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.decisive_experiment: Tracking accelerometer readings inside a vehicle rounding a curve at constant speedometer speed: accelerometer registers substantial lateral centripetal acceleration.

cognitive_conflict_matrix.intuitive_misconception: When moving forward through rain, the rain hits you from behind because you run into the air.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.newtonian_scientific_truth: The apparent velocity of rain relative to you is v_{rain/man} = v_{rain} - v_{man}. Since v_{man} is forward (+x), -v_{man} is backward (-x), causing the rain to arrive slanted from the front, requiring you to tilt your umbrella forward.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.decisive_experiment: Walking in vertically falling rain: dry front of shirt gets soaked while back remains dry unless umbrella is tilted forward.
